question.knowledge_point: Further Determining Rates of Change in Geometrical Settings
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14004055/assets/4915dc00f10fa5edc911cf9744e99e662b705898b32f16391805c7733b8f89e5.png)

The surface area $A$ of the sphere above is increasing. The radius of the sphere is $r.$ Find the rate of change of the surface area of a sphere with respect to its radius.
question.worked_solution:
The area of the surface area of the sphere is given by  

$$
A=A(r)=4\pi {r}^{2}
$$

where $r$ is the radius of the sphere.

Therefore, the rate of change of $A(r)$ with respect to its radius $r$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{′}(r) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}r}(4\pi {r}^{2}) \\  & =4\pi (2r) \\  & =8\pi r.\end{aligned}
$$
